items.title: Fortis Games Closes With Over 400 Jobs Impacted
items.excerpt: Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs.
items.content_text: Fortis Games, a studio behind mobile titles like Twilight Towers and Bloom & Breakfast, has closed its doors, impacting around 440 jobs. CEO Steven Chiang confirmed the closure in a statement to GamesBeat on November 10, 2026. “Fortis has been a labor of love for so many of us and we’re disappointed we weren’t able to achieve the goals we set for ourselves when we started this journey more than five years ago,” he told the outlet. “We have been fortunate to work with some of the most talented and dedicated people in this space. As we move forward, our primary focus will be on helping this talented team of individuals find new opportunities. Thank you to everyone who has supported us over the past five years. We are grateful for the collaboration and friendship we have shared with so many.” Several former employees have spoken out about the closure in posts on LinkedIn. In one of these posts, game producer Gustavo Coronet confirmed that Las Vegas Sands Corp., Fortis Games’ parent company, chose to “end funding and part ways, terminating all of the contracts, worldwide.” “Super proud of the work we’ve done. LVS’s decision does not delete the ground breaking and best-in class agentic development workflow the Octopus team has built, nor the massively solid soft launch metrics both our projects were achieving in such early stages of development,” he wrote. In another post, former communications director Scott Butterworth suggested that Fortis’s “community-focused” approach to mobile games didn’t resonate enough with players to help it “get off the ground.” “Ah, Fortis Games — what could have been. Despite our unique, community-focused approach to the mobile games market, we just couldn't seem to get off the ground, and today, we finally ran out of runway,” he wrote. “The company has officially shuttered, abruptly putting more than 400 talented people out of work (myself included). Hilariously, I'm also in the process of relocating to Los Angeles, so hey, why not add a little more change on top, right?” Fortis Gaming was founded in 2022 by Steven Chiang, former executive at Electronic Arts and Zynga. Based out of San Francisco, California, it was funded by Las Vegas Sands Corp. to help the casino brand expand outside of gambling. Fortis went on to acquire several games studios over the ensuing four years; on November 4, it announced that it was sunsetting Twilight Towers , a move that came a mere week before Fortis’s total closure. This is the latest game studio to shut its doors after EA revealed that it had closed down BioWare , famous for AAA RPG series like Mass Effect and Dragon Age — a decision that has proven to be extremely unpopular among players, who are now campaigning for EA to do something , anything, with its IP to prevent them from languishing in obscurity.

items.title: The DCU Regime Change Threatens to Turn Man of Tomorrow Into 2027’s Answer to The Flash
items.excerpt: It’s been four years since James Gunn and Peter Safran were announced as the co-bosses of DC Studios, and just a day since their ouster was revealed, and we're having a serious case of déjà vu.
items.content_text: It’s fall 2022 and a new regime is announced as taking over DC’s film and TV future even as a major DC movie from the prior regime continues in post-production for release the following summer. It’s fall 2026 and a new regime is announced as taking over DC’s film and TV future even as a major DC movie from the prior regime continues in post-production for release the following summer. It’s been four years since James Gunn and Peter Safran were announced as the co-bosses of DC Studios, and just a day since their ouster was revealed, and this nerd reporter is having a serious case of déjà vu. When Gunn and Safran took the reins of DC in October 2022, they were inheriting several projects that were already far into production: the headline-plagued The Flash , Blue Beetle , and Batgirl . In 2023, The Flash marked the end of a DC film continuity created just a handful of years earlier — the DCEU, aka the Snyderverse — that would see a group of DC heroes, including Supergirl, band together to stop a cosmic threat to Earth led by one of Superman’s greatest foes. In 2027, Man of Tomorrow will potentially mark the end of a DC film continuity created just a handful of years earlier — the DCU — that will see a group of DC heroes, including Supergirl , band together to stop a cosmic threat to Earth led by one of Superman’s greatest foes. The Flash had its heroes out to stop General Zod, while Man of Tomorrow will feature Brainiac (in his live-action film debut). The parallels between the end of Snyder’s DCEU and Gunn’s DCU are depressingly similar. In both cases, new regimes were taking hold of the reins of Warner Bros. and resetting the priorities of its most important superhero IP with little regard to the projects and characters that fans had been conditioned to believe were going to matter going forward. The regime change of 2022 told fans that the upcoming DC films no longer mattered because they would be ret-conned out of the next iteration of the DC Universe. More DC Studios News: Batman, Wonder Woman Prioritized Which Project Could Get Batgirl'd? No Season 2 for Lanterns Skydance Was Unhappy With DCU Box Office DCU's Batman Was Dead Before It Was Born Is that where we’re at now with the DCU? Until newly appointed DC Studios boss Jeremy Latcham says otherwise, fans can only suspect we’re back to square one again with upcoming DC projects (unless they heed some fans’ advice not to reboot the DCU again). If that’s it for Gunn and Safran’s “Gods and Monsters,” then why should fans be invested in Man of Tomorrow if it no longer matters? It will just collapse in on itself as The Flash did. I was at Warner Bros. in late January 2023 when James Gunn and Peter Safran announced their “Gods and Monsters” roadmap . Even then, the invited press, myself included, couldn’t mask our doubts. Haven’t we seen these big presentations and slate reveals before only for them to never materialize? (I was also at a San Diego Comic-Con panel when DC announced a Cyborg solo film , which obviously never happened.) At that launch event, Gunn and Safran did their best to persuade us that this time would be different. Sadly, it wasn’t. Whatever plans the new DC Studios regime under Jeremy Latcham announces should be met with a comparable degree of skepticism because it could all be over, once again, in a Flash.

items.title: Lanterns Not Renewed for Season 2, Says DC Studios Insider
items.excerpt: An insider at DC Studios claims that HBO’s Lanterns was not renewed for a second season in spite of rave reviews and audience interest, as told in a report from Variety.
items.content_text: An insider at DC Studios claims that HBO’s Lanterns was not renewed for a second season in spite of rave reviews and audience interest, as told in a report from Variety. Variety’s report comes on the heels of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s exit from DC Studios on Monday, November 9. In a statement to the public, Gunn cited a dislike for the more “corporate” aspect of his position, citing long hours that negatively impacted his personal relationships. Unsurprisingly, fans are now worried about the future of the DCU, given that Gunn had only been in his role for four years with just three films to show for it. Superman was released to generally positive reception; Supergirl decidedly less so; Clayface was also a mixed bag, but Lanterns , the live-action show that released on HBO this year, was a massive success . Boasting viewership numbers that rivaled the likes of The Pitt , it’s safe to say that audiences loved Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart, and hopes were high for a second season. In fact, it seemed almost inevitable — but, according to insiders, it didn’t quite “capture the zeitgeist.” Whatever that means. Variety’s report says this insider pointed out that the series “didn’t get renewed for a second season,” telling the outlet, “People cannot wait to make another season of a hit show.” This news, if true, comes as quite a shock — but that seems to be the theme of the month, given Safran and Gunn’s unexpected exit. In October, series co-creator Damon Lindelof revealed that writers were already hashing out ideas for a second season , though it hadn’t been greenlit just yet. Safran confirmed this news in an October interview with IGN , though he admitted that it hinged on whether or not the team could come up with a story worth following up from the first season. "The episodic world is always going to be a really important part of our overall slate, it's a great way to tell stories that need more real estate than a feature film can offer you, and it's a great way to introduce characters that we then bring into the feature world," Safran told us. "And I think that Aaron Pierre and John Stewart are a perfect example of that. We introduced him in Lanterns, and audiences will see him next summer in Man of Tomorrow. So, it's really important to us in continuing to tell aspects of the story that we're not telling in the feature film world, so there's more to come. "Listen, we'll see what happens with Lanterns Season 2. If, I think, the collective group of HBO and DC and Chris Mundy and the team all feel like we've got something that is a worthy successor to quite a beloved first season of television, then I wouldn't be surprised to see more." While official news on the future of Lanterns remains up in the air, this report paints a grim picture for the future of the DCU which was, somewhat tragically, only just getting started.

items.title: Shaquille O'Neal is Starring in a Game Show Where Players Have to Hide Him in Plain Sight
items.excerpt: In one of the more amusing sidequests that Shaquille O’Neal has undertaken in his life, the former NBA All-Star is set to appear in a game show where players try to conceal him from view in a hilarious twist on hide-and-seek.
items.content_text: In one of the more amusing sidequests that Shaquille O’Neal has embarked on in his life, the former NBA All-Star is set to appear in a game show where players try to conceal him from view in a hilarious twist on hide-and-seek. Can You Hide… Shaq? Is the name of this upcoming game show, which will premiere with two episodes at 9 PM on Thursday, December 3, on ABC and the ESPN app. Episodes will be available to stream on Hulu starting December 4. The show pits two teams of contestants against each other, challenging them to hide Shaq in plain sight in public areas around Dallas, Texas. This is no small feat, given that Shaq is a massive former athlete and one of the world's most recognizable celebrities. “I’m 7-foot-1. I’m not exactly easy to miss,” Shaquille O’Neal said, per Variety . “I love meeting people wherever I go, but for years I’ve always wondered, could somebody actually make me disappear? Well, we finally decided to put it to the test. We turned it into a real competition, and I can’t wait for you to see the creative, ridiculous ways they tried to hide me in plain sight. The stakes are high, and so is the prize. But you know me, we’re gonna have some fun along the way.” Comedian Nicole Byer will host the program, which promises to be a competition full of “fast, funny, and unpredictable challenges.” The show's logline lays out the rules: “Contestants first split into two teams, each with a set mission and time clock. The team that completes its mission with the fewest spottings earns immunity for one team member in the next round, who then becomes team captain. The teams must work together toward one greater mission: earning prize money to add to the ‘Shaq-pot’ that will ultimately be claimed by one winner.” As of yet, the amount in the ‘Shaq-pot’ is unknown, but it had better be worth it, given how undoubtedly difficult it is to disguise one of the NBA’s most famous players. Can you hide… Shaq? Is produced by Jersey Legends Productions and Fulwell Entertainment in partnership with ESPN. Executive producers listed are Shaquille O’Neal, Colin Smeeton, Jeremy Castro, Charlie Van Vleet, Adam Cooper, Ben Winston, Mike Paris, and Emma Conway. Shaq has undertaken no small amount of passion projects in his career; aside from his legacy as a sports legend, he's also a dubstep artist (under the name DJ Diesel), rapper, actor, and has even appeared in a few video games, including Fortnite and of course, Shaq Fu . I personally can't wait to see how contestants manage to hide Shaq in this show. Let us know what your strategy would be in the comments, and whether or not you'll be watching come December 3. items.title: I Tried the Pokémon Happy Meal — Here’s What I Learned (and What I Pulled)
items.content_text: Pokémon Happy Meals have officially returned, and if the swarm of teenagers in my generally quiet local McDonald’s is anything to go by, they’re bigger than ever. The Pokémon Company first announced the return of its McDonald's promotion several weeks back, causing some confusion by accidentally spoiling next year’s promo card list . Good times. Now that I’ve gotten my hands on the 30th Anniversary Happy Meal, I can confirm the previously leaked card set is in fact the accurate one, along with new details about the promotion’s roll-out. The Pokémon Happy Meal is available in all of McDonald’s traditional Happy Meal variants: hamburger, cheeseburger, or 4 and 6-piece nugget combos. Prices vary based on your meal selection, but every option comes with the same packaging and blind-boxed toys. I was surprised to find how little my local McDonald’s was seemingly marketing the collab, which presumably varies across locations. My McDonald’s only had one poster, and otherwise sporadically flashed the Pokémon Happy Meal teaser on its digital ordering screens. For reference, when I went to Target’s Pokémon launch , the whole store was covered in Pokémon materials. Many of these posters and stands ended up on eBay , so it’s possible TPC is now limiting its 'physical' marketing footprint to help stores avoid any tussles or, you know, crime. While some social media users are claiming their local McDonald’s is approaching the collab as a progressive roll-out, my local D.C. McDonald’s had all three boxes and 15 promo cards ready to go. A staff member, however, did acknowledge that other stores may be receiving the promotional materials "in batches." Given the swarms of kids and teenagers who had seemingly abandoned school for Pokémon, I was only willing to pick up two Happy Meals. (A six-nugget and a cheeseburger, in case you were curious.) The working manager was kind enough to ensure I got two different Pokémon boxes, which ended up being Torchic and Pikachu. I quickly realized that was a strategic choice — almost every other customer was specifically requesting (and getting) the Umbreon box, so the staff was trying to manage its stock. Of course, one of the main draws of the collaboration is new promo cards, which often end up reselling at the same price as the Happy Meal itself. While rumors had already been circulating online, I was still shocked to discover they really do give you the two promo cards without any packaging. They’re slipped into a box right next to a hard plastic toy that, for whatever reason, does get delicate tissue paper wrapping. The box, at least, is definitely serviceable for storing decks. I’ll admit the lack of packaging does make the card reveal less climactic, and I can imagine there’s already someone complaining out there about getting a damaged card. Still, I don’t mind Pokemon treating its promo cards a little more casually in the interest of promoting the TCG as a game to be played as opposed to a collector’s racket. I anti-climactically slid out Eevee and Tyranitaur from my first box, then found Zoroark and Chandelure in my second one. Each card is a reprint marked with the M26 label and its own numbering system, and some have holo foil. You can see the (real) full list of 2026 promo cards here . The other toy you get is a miniature plastic version of the Happy Meal box themed after an individual Pokémon, with the full slate shown below. Each toy box has a clip you can use to attach it to a bag or keychain, and I happened to get Diglit and good ol' Pikachu. This is far from Pokémon’s first time teaming up with the fast-food giant. The partnership goes all the way back to 1999, when Pokémania first hit its stride. The modern 'Pokémon Happy Meal' first launched in 2011. It was only natural that the promotion would return for the year of Pokémon’s 30th anniversary, offering what I believe to be one of the best budget-friendly ways for fans to get involved in the festivities. Safe to say, I'm satisfied, albeit still hungry. The Pokémon Happy Meal is now available across all U.S. McDonald’s locations through December 14. The promotion will be expanding to additional countries over the next couple of months, with the full roll-out detailed in an official McDonald’s post .
items.title_en: I Tried the Pokémon Happy Meal — Here’s What I Learned (and What I Pulled)

items.title: We Asked Nintendo of America's Nate Bihldorff About Localizing Ocarina of Time's Most Obscure Secrets
items.excerpt: "The localization team, absolutely, puts the most importance on those single lines that are really, really hard to find."
items.content_text: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is filled with little pieces of dialogue tucked away in secret moments. You can trigger them by talking to a character at a very specific point in time, getting an item out of order and seeing how characters react, and various other ways. There are dozens of interactions that are really easy to miss: I’m on my third playthrough of the remake and am still stumbling into lines of dialogue I didn’t see the first two times around. During a launch event at Nintendo’s New York retail store, I spoke with Nate Bihldorff, Senior Vice President of Product Development and Publishing at Nintendo of America, and asked about how the localization team approaches these small moments. “My group handles the localization of these games," Bihldorff said. "And I can tell you that the localization team, absolutely, puts the most importance on those single lines that are really, really hard to find. And you know, of course, they are murder on testing teams because finding that specific line and making sure that it appears correctly in the game is super important… But there was always something special about localizing those lines and knowing that only a few people were going to read it, that it took a specific course of action to get there, whether it's in a Zelda game like this or you’re sequence breaking in a Metroid game. "There was always something special about localizing those lines and knowing that only a few people were going to read it..." "Knowing that the person who's experiencing that line did something special to get it and wanting to make sure that it had that little extra oomph, I guarantee you the localization team would love to hear you say exactly that… You feel like you're connecting with the developers in those moments. It's a direct line where they're kind of winking at you.” With so many secrets that exist just for the joy of being secrets, I can’t help but wonder if there are things in Ocarina of Time that no one has found yet. While Bihldorff is quick to point out that he can’t speak on behalf of the developers, he personally likes to think there’s still something hiding in Ocarina of Time that’s a secret to everybody. “I like to believe that there are. Of course, that's a question for the developers. They probably would be very cagey in the way that they answered it. But I also feel like Nintendo games in general have a wondrous way of having something that you just don't discover forever.” Part of the reason Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma wanted to develop a remake of Ocarina of Time was so younger developers at Nintendo could familiarize themselves with one of the company’s most influential games. Developers with different levels of experience with the original Ocarina of Time came together to create its Switch 2 remake. Across the Pacific Ocean, the localization team at Nintendo of America had a similar experience. “As someone who was also around for the original, I feel like it was almost doubly meaningful because you really feel the opportunity to not only be a part of something that was so meaningful for a previous generation of fans, but also be there at the moment that a new generation who had never played it before are going to experience it in really this unbelievably beautiful and well thought-out state.” Internally at Nintendo of America, Bihldorff said that mix of generations led to different perspectives during localization: “You get to talk to somebody who maybe worked on the original game, and the IP has a specific meaning for [them], and then, a younger staff who's maybe coming in right out of school in their early 20s who, of course they've heard of it, but I'm seeing them experiencing these things for the first time… That sort of estuary water mix I think is something that's really, really important for the creative process, and it keeps this company vibrant. It's certainly something that I feed off of.” The sense of anticipation was obvious as Nintendo employees prepared for the midnight launch while fans lined up outside. Nintendo of America is a very secretive place, and I’m always curious to learn what the process is like when they first get word of what the developers in Japan are working on years before a public event like this. “I think it's not me pulling the curtain too far back to be able to say that every single one of these games is met with tremendous enthusiasm the second we hear about them. It’s a tough job sometimes, being behind the scenes when you can't talk to anybody. We don't talk to our spouses and stuff like that about it. It's a lot of secret stuff. And yet we're also passionate about the work and, of course, making sure that we bring the developers’ visions to market in a way that makes it proud. Everybody takes it very seriously, but they're also huge fans. So yeah, I can say, absolute excitement when we heard about this.” After years of working in secrecy, Nintendo now hands Ocarina of Time off to the fans. One such fan at the launch event was Grammy, Oscar, and Emmy-winning musician Jon Batiste, who spoke to me about how The Legend of Zelda’s music influenced him from a young age, starting with Link’s Awakening on the Game Boy. “When I was a kid and my sister, who was really my hero, she had a Game Boy and we would play. Every day, we rode up and down the street and she would play first, and then when the battery was almost out, she would give it to me and I would play until the battery ran completely out," Batiste said. "And I realized at that point, okay, I'm pretty much going to be doing this for the rest of my life. “And then when I started to play Nintendo 64, that's when I started with Ocarina of Time and the music captured me. And I started to actually play those scores on instruments. And I played tons of scores from Nintendo games on the piano. My cousin and I actually, we have a video of us as a band when we first started playing, and our repertoire was probably 50% Nintendo franchise themes. So then we started to research who were the composers of the scores and we started to really pick favorites, like Koji Kondo. The sound of those melodies, I would say, was an early compositional influence.” For more on The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, check out my interview with producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi . And, read about the launch event on the other coast, where Ryan McCaffrey spoke to Nintendo of America’s Bill Trinen .

items.title: Nintendo Opens New Job Role to Preserve and Organize its Old Games
items.excerpt: Nintendo of America has opened up a new job position to help preserve and archive the older games in its vast library of titles.
items.content_text: Nintendo of America has opened up a new job position to help preserve and archive the older games in its vast library. Nintendo has released around 11,000 games in its lifetime. Now, it’s looking to organize those games — at least, the older ones — with a specialized role at its Redmond, WA location. As per the official job description , Nintendo of America’s future Digital Archivist, Historical Systems will support the “preservation, organization, and accessibility of historical hardware and software information” by designing and implementing a “structured framework for organizing technical records, engineering documentation, source materials, and institutional knowledge related to legacy systems and platforms.” Essentially, the digital archivist is a librarian of sorts, whose job is to create a means of organizing and documenting all of Nintendo’s older games, systems, and platforms, as well as any documentation or materials related to them. It definitely sounds like a fun role for video game history buffs, especially if they like organizing data. The job listing describes its ideal candidate as someone with “expertise in archives, metadata management, information architecture, and research” who will work “closely with subject matter experts across engineering, product development, legal, and business teams” to “establish standards and processes that ensure historical information remains discoverable, usable, and preserved for future generations.” The position is a 12-month contract role with a salary of $35-$55 per hour. A Bachelor’s degree in library & information science, Archives, Museum Studies, Information Management, History, Technical Communication, or a related field is preferred, although equivalent professional experience may be considered. This is a major step forward for video game preservation, something that activists and enthusiasts in the space have been calling for for some time now. For example, the Video Game History Foundation was founded in 2016 with the intent of preserving and teaching the history of video games. Since then, it has worked toward creating the United States’ first dedicated library for the study of video game history, as well as preserving games’ source code. Given Nintendo’s relevance in the games industry and its role in the history of the medium, it makes sense that the company would seek to archive its works. Perhaps this could result in some unexpected discoveries; for example, one collector came across 97 copies of an unreleased version of Super Mario Bros. Duck Hunt earlier this year, five of which were graded perfect 10s by PSA.

items.title: DC's New Leader Will Reportedly Prioritize More Well-Known Characters Like Batman and Wonder Woman, Reboot Has Yet to Be Decided
items.excerpt: DC Studios' new boss is reportedly planning to prioritize more mainstream characters like Batman and Wonder Woman going forward.
items.content_text: DC Studios' new boss is reportedly planning to prioritize more mainstream characters like Batman and Wonder Woman going forward. Earlier this week, it was announced that DC Studios heads James Gunn and Peter Safran were stepping down (reports indicate they were actually fired ), and now... we have an idea of what the new direction for the franchise may look like. According to a new report from The Wrap , DC Studios' new incoming CEO, Jeremy Latcham, is expected to focus only on the hits going forward. The report claims that Latcham has been tasked by Skydance CEO David Ellison to assemble the Justice League on the big screen as quickly as possible. That means prioritizing projects with The Flash, Wonder Woman, Batman, and other heroes that the average filmgoer would recognize. As a result, don't expect bigger swings with more niche characters like Clayface, Booster Gold, or Peacemaker. The report even name-checked "modest" characters like Supergirl as not being a focus going forward. As of right now, DC has yet to decide if they will need to wipe the slate clean again and do a full reboot, with new actors and storylines. The universe is still so young and has yet to interconnect with all of its installments, so there's room to pivot... and it would be a PR disaster to recast David Corenswet after also publicly dumping Henry Cavill just a few years ago . The focus on mainstream characters is the direct inverse of James Gunn's style, as he really rose in prominence with Guardians of the Galaxy, a film about a group of misfits that the general audience wasn't very familiar with. Gunn tried to extend that to the DCU to mixed results. Many have been wondering where Gunn's Batman is, particularly after he was a no-show in Clayface. Gunn did open this universe with Superman, and a sequel is on the way, but it's not quite enough for fans. The early slate of projects has led to frustrations among viewers that Gunn isn't building enough momentum to bring the biggest characters to the center of the DCU. Ironically, Gunn had recently stated that Superman, Wonder Woman, and Batman were going to be pivotal to the DCU , so it seems he was building to it, but seemingly not fast enough for Skydance. The Wrap also noted that Latcham will refrain from having a big social media presence, as Gunn was known for being active to a fault. Although he would answer fan questions, he would also sometimes create confusion, get into feuds with fans, and it didn't always create the best image of DC. It's unclear what the next era of DC will look like, but hopefully it's not as chaotic and tumultuous as fans are expecting, since this franchise has been through enough already.

items.title: World of Warcraft Forever Hotfix Will Thin Out Overcrowded Zones and Help Faction Balance
items.excerpt: World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players. And, Blizzard has implemented a fix.
items.content_text: World of Warcraft Forever has been incredibly popular, and has gone down as the biggest WoW launch in history. It's little wonder, then, that some zones are absolutely packed with players — but thankfully, Blizzard has implemented a fix. In a hotfix last night , Blizzard lowered the population in overcrowded zones, which should give players more of a chance to get quests done without competing with a hundred other players to tag a spider. In the developers' notes, Blizzard also noted that "We’ve made this an even bigger change on the PvP ruleset, following feedback from players that they felt overcrowded in several places. We will continue to monitor how zones feel and make further adjustments as necessary." Unlike past versions of WoW, which had a variety of servers available, World of Warcraft Forever has one server that's divided into different rulesets: PvP, PvE, RPPvP, RP and Hardcore. Instead of dividing players among different servers, Blizzard uses layering to group people into different instances of the world. And because WoW Forever's whole thing is being surrounded by other players, Blizzard seemingly opted to try and get as many people into each layer as possible without causing problems. However, while it's fun to see hundreds of players running around each zone, this approach has caused some issues. Some people on the PvE rulesets have reported difficulties in being able to finish quests, especially in the earlier zones, as they have to compete with dozens of different players to get anything done. But the problem is especially bad for players in the PvP rulesets because of a faction imbalance. At least here in the US, The Horde is much more popular than The Alliance, and that's causing problems. For Alliance players, they're outnumbered when they're questing in the world, which means they get killed instantly in later zones. For Horde players, they can't create new toons, because Blizzard is throttling character creation to try and preserve faction balance. Blizzard Community Manager Kaivax has addressed this in a seperate note last night , saying, "It’s vitally important that the PvP rulesets in WoW: Forever have balanced factions where both factions vie for supremacy, creating memories of epic victories and stunning defeats that we all remember for years to come. While even the most extreme case in a region is currently at roughly a 55/45 split, that is not as close as we want it to be." Blizzard wants to get that balance as close to 50/50 as possible. To address the matter, Kaivax says, "In the short term, that means that it will become increasingly difficult to create characters on the more populous faction in each region – currently Horde on North American PvP rulesets or Alliance in EU Roleplay-PvP. As everyone settles and shifts, these may flip to the other side." Despite some of these growing pains, though, World of Warcraft Forever is still proving to be one of the smoothest launches in Blizzard history. Launch night went off without a hitch , thanks to the servers running on around 251TB of RAM and over 70,000 CPU cores. items.title: PlayStation Cancels Live-Service Heist Shooter, Fairgames
items.excerpt: Fairgames, a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony.
items.content_text: Fairgames , a live-service heist game from PlayStation's Haven Studios, has been canceled by Sony. A new report from Bloomberg reveals that Fairgames has been scrapped, three and a half years after its announcement. Developer Haven Studios will not be shut down, nor will there be any layoffs, as PlayStation has decided to turn the team into a support studio for other first-party projects. The decision to pull the plug on the game was made after a recent test did not meet internal expectations. “While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” said executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in a note reviewed by Bloomberg. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.” The test being referenced here is likely one that made some waves earlier this fall. A mysterious game known as Project Espresso, which looked a lot like Fairgames, began advertising private playtests with a gameplay trailer back in September . Not much is known about those tests, but they didn't seem to be very fruitful for the team. Fairgames was announced in 2023 and has been the subject of scrutiny for some time. Some fans pushed back on PlayStation's live-service pivot during the early 2020s, as the company has always excelled with blockbuster single-player games. When Concord bombed , fans began to express even further revulsion toward titles like Fairgames. The project has also been soured by a number of setbacks, including departures of key developers and internal struggles . Fairgames' cancelation marks yet another major failure for PlayStation's live-service efforts. Concord flopped, The Last of Us Online was scrapped , an online God of War game was killed , and Marathon has been struggling since launch. Helldivers 2, on the other hand, has been a big win for PlayStation. There's some hope that maybe Bungie's decision to revive Destiny 2 could be productive , but Sony seems to be moving away from live-service. The only other major live-service game from PlayStation on the horizon is 4:Loop , a new game from JJ Abrams' studio, Bad Robot. We'll see if it suffers a similar fate as these other titles.

items.title: We Build LEGO Downton Abbey, a Stately Set That's Worthy of the Crawley Name
items.excerpt: We build LEGO Ideas Downton Abbey, a big, heavy, stately set that comes with 13 minifigures.
items.content_text: I like Julian Fellowes’ current HBO show The Gilded Age just fine, with its American characters’ focus on social striving and entrepreneurial success. But I suspect I'll always prefer Fellowes’ previous show, Downton Abbey. It’s a British historical drama that takes place as the era of landed aristocracy evolves into a more modern, fluid class structure. With its enormous cast of characters you want to root for – both the aristocratic Crawleys as well as the servants – watching Downton Abbey is like a warm hug. Release Date : October 1, 2026 Price : $349.99 Pieces : 4,711 Ages : 18+ Set # : 21373 Dimensions : Height: 12" (30cm), Width: 18" (44cm), Depth: 7" (16cm) I’ve seen the full run of Downton Abbey more than once – I’m talking all six seasons of the show, plus the three follow-up movies. I even recently bought the Ultimate Legacy Collection , which means another rewatch is likely in the near future (after the fourth season of The Gilded Age concludes, anyway). During the hundred-plus hours I’ve spent in the company of the Crawleys and co., I’ve become intimately familiar with the rooms and architecture of the massive building of the title. Downton Abbey is where the series’ massive cast of characters live and work. It’s where they clash with each other and make up (or don’t). It’s where they get sick and die (or get better). It’s where they fret about money, or get sent off to war, or make major life decisions that will affect their futures. It’s where they live their eventful early 20th-century lives. The fictional building Downton Abbey is based on (and often filmed at) the very real Highclere Castle , which was built in 1679 in southern England. It’s a sprawling manor that has three full floors, with towers springing from the corners and center of the building. LEGO Ideas Downton Abbey ( see it at LEGO ) stays true to the real castle’s design, but shrinks it down to minifigure scale, with just two main stories and the towers. Rather than depicting the entire building, which would likely be tedious to build and hide the interior rooms, the set focuses on the front facade. The back of the set is open to reveal six rooms anyone who’s watched the show would recognize. Shrinking Downton Abbey down this way works beautifully. The exterior is finely detailed, with over a dozen windows, as well as downspouts, pinnacles, and an ornate heraldic stone portico over the entrance, just like the real castle. Building such a large set took me many hours, over the course of a couple of weeks. It’s comprised of nearly 5,000 pieces, with the bricks divided into 35 bags and the building instructions separated into two books. Despite the time it takes, the build itself is generally enjoyable, especially when you’re making all the little furniture and items that bring the rooms to life. Just like in the show, the interior of LEGO Downton Abbey are divided between the “upstairs,” where the Crawleys live and work, and the “downstairs,” where the domestic servants prepare the food and take their breaks. Upstairs are the Crawley’s dining room, main hall, and grand library. Downstairs are the kitchen, servants' hall, and the office of Carson the butler. The set is large overall, but dividing two floors into six rooms means each room is relatively small. The LEGO designers have made the most of the space, packing lots of distinctive details into each area. Upstairs, the grand library alone has bookcases and curtains lining the walls, as well as a couch, a pot of flowers, a writing desk, and a fireplace. Downstairs, the servants’ hall has two rows of bells on one wall, just like you see in the opening credits of the show. In Carson’s office, his desk is adorned with a wine decanter, a lamp, and an old-school telephone. It’s always fun to see how just a few bricks can transform into an identifiable object in the house. Since Downton Abbey has a notably large cast of characters, it’s only fitting that this LEGO set comes with a slew of minifigures. You get 13 in all, including most of the main characters we follow throughout the series. All of the women in dresses come with an alternate pair of legs that allow them to sit down as well. Minifigures Included Dowager Countess Lord Grantham Lady Grantham Lady Mary Lady Edith Tom Branson Mr Carson Mrs Hughes Mr Bates Anna Bates Thomas Barrow Mrs Patmore Daisy Parker The only part of the set that’s somewhat of a drag to build is the exterior walls, which are made of lots of repeated parts. This is a big, heavy set, and to sustain the weight, the walls have to be structurally sound. That means you have to build lots of the same thick, complex corner pieces to situate throughout the build. This is to be expected in a set based on a large building, but I found doing just a bag or two a day helped ward off the potential boredom. Once the build is complete, the entire second story of the house can be lifted neatly off, giving you easy access to the lower interior rooms. The floors of both levels are sturdily built; they feel strong enough that you can move each story of the manor without worrying that the whole thing will fall apart in your hands. The final piece of the build is the bench that sits under the cedar tree near the manor. In the show, you’ll often find Lady Mary sitting there, or the Dowager Countess. I realize you have to be a pretty die-hard Downton Abbey fan to drop $349.99 on a LEGO set. But if you are, and you have the cash, you won't regret picking it up. It’s intricately designed, with lots of notable details from the show. It’s a largely enjoyable (if occasionally tedious) build, and the large cast of minifigures is delightful and full of personality. I enjoyed my time with this set as one more way to immerse myself in the world of Downton Abbey, at least until my next binge through the show. LEGO Ideas Downton Abbey is available exclusively through the LEGO Store .

items.title: Someone Got Halo 1 Running on a Sega Dreamcast
items.excerpt: A developer has successfully gotten the original Halo: Combat Evolved, a day-one launch title for the original Xbox in 2001, ported and running on the Sega Dreamcast – in both campaign and multiplayer. And they've posted 28 minutes of gameplay footage from the campaign and multiplayer to prove it.
items.content_text: A developer has successfully gotten the original Halo: Combat Evolved, a day-one launch title for the original Xbox in 2001, ported and running on the Sega Dreamcast – in both campaign and multiplayer. And he's posted 28 minutes of gameplay footage from the campaign and multiplayer to prove it. X user and game developer "Jilted Valkyrie" uploaded the footage just days ahead of the 25th anniversary of both Halo and the Xbox itself. The Dreamcast, meanwhile, is a tad older, having launched in Japan in late 1998 and worldwide in late 1999. The footage shows a modified title screen displaying the title, "Halo: Dreamcast Evolved," with the legendary Halo theme music playing. It then shows multiplayer footage on a number of maps, including big ones like Sidewinder. Meanwhile, footage from the first mission of the campaign is there too. The framerate appears to dip below 30fps at times, but it doesn't take away from the technical marvel that is getting an Xbox game running on the older Dreamcast hardware. Jilted Valkyrie says the campaign port is currently 77% complete, and he shouts out Dreamcast developer Falco Girgis for his help on the project. "If you like what you see, go give @falco_girgis a follow. Without his work in KOS and SH4ZAM, this unique, passionate port of Halo would not exist. He inspired me with his technical posts on GTA3 for Dreamcast to do something I always wondered about... Halo on Sega." He later added, "It's not a 1:1 port, so the experience has completely new things to it not in any other version. There's even an entire new mode... plus who wouldn't want to play Halo online on Dreamcast?" He did not give details on the new mode, however. Finally, he says that he expects to release it this year. As for modern Halo, Xbox seems set to reboot the franchise – or at the very least, the way Halo is made. Xbox leadership took development duties on the next mainline Halo away from Halo Studios (nee 343 Industries) and handed them to Activision , who will form a new team to helm the project. It's a bold move, and it remains to be seen if it can restore the series to its former glory .

items.title: Today’s Top Deals: Astro Bot, Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 SE Mouse, and Star Wars Galactic Racer

items.content_text: Amazon just dropped the details on its Black Friday sale , and some early deals are already live. You can save on LEGO Star Wars , an animatronic Pikachu Plush , Astro Bot , and more. Those aren’t the only highlights today; the Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 SE is half off, you can save $32 on a $200 Nintendo eShop Gift Card , and more. TL;DR - The Best Deals for November 10 Over $20 Off Astro Bot Astro Bot is over $20 off on Amazon and Walmart, marking its biggest discount in months. Earning IGN’s Game of the Year Award in 2024 , it’s one of the best 3D platformers ever made, full of PlayStation nostalgia, and sure to be fun for the whole family. In IGN’s Astro Bot review , Simon Cardy found that with the “collection of endlessly inventive levels and fantastically fun abilities, it delivers joy in spades, never once becoming even remotely dull or repetitive.” $70 Off the Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 SE Gaming Mouse The red Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 SE Gaming Mouse is just $69 at Walmart. It’s an incredibly lightweight gaming mouse with an advanced optical sensor that tracks over 888+ IPS and up to 44,000 DPI. The switches are precise and reliable, and the 88-hour battery with USB-C charging is a nice addition. Read IGN’s full review of the Logitech G PRO X Superlight 2 to learn more; it’s nearly identical to the SE model but offers an 8,000Hz polling rate instead of 1,000Hz. Save on Star Wars Galactic Racer Star Wars: Galactic Racer for PC dropped last month and is now $46.99 with the code “SSF74449” at checkout on Newegg. You’ll receive a Steam code shortly after purchase to redeem and start playing. In IGN’s review , Luke Reilly said, “Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous-looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that impressively goes further than just taking the decades-old Star Wars Racer games and giving them a 4K facelift.” The racing game also features an interesting roguelite campaign structure. If you’re looking to play on PS5, the Deluxe Edition is $8 off at Amazon and Target. Beyond the base game, you get a few digital and physical bonuses, including a digital art book, a Naboo N-1 Starfighter livery, three arcade events, and more. Get $32 Off a $200 Nintendo eShop Gift Card A $200 Nintendo eShop Gift Card is down to $168 on Newegg with the code “BNWF2674”. Beyond buying games, DLC, online memberships, and in-game currency in the eShop, you can use it on hardware from the Nintendo Store. However, the wallet limit is $800. It’s the best way to save on items that aren’t discounted, including The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. MTG x The Hobbit Treasures of Smaug Scene Box In Stock at MSRP The MTG x The Hobbit Treasures of Smaug Scene Box is back in stock at MSRP, shipped and sold by Amazon. Inside, you’ll find six Borderless Scene cards, all playable, and six art-only cards you can put on display using the included easel. Rounding out the collection are three Play Boosters. Get a Nintendo Switch 2 for $418 You can get a brand-new US version of the Nintendo Switch 2 for $417.87 on AliExpress when you use the code "USAFF95" at checkout. This deal is for new AliExpress customers; existing customers get it for $429.87. The seller, Lucky Tech Store, is legit and sells other gaming consoles and more. Since there are no guarantees the Switch 2 will get a Black Friday discount, this is the best deal on the console, especially after the September price hike. Even if the Switch 2 goes on sale, the deals will likely be on bundles. Get Half Off the Elgato Wave Neo Microphone Looking to up your streaming game for cheap. The Elgato Wave Neo Microphone is down to just $45.99 at Best Buy. This plug-and-play USB-C condenser microphone is great for beginners. It sounds significantly better than a headset mic, works seamlessly with almost all platforms, and its cardioid pattern picks up your voice while rejecting background noise. I have an Elgato microphone myself and love it, and to get one this cheap is a steal. Save 55% on the New Animatronic Pikachu Plush The Puppetronics Pikachu is back down to just $35.99 when you clip the coupon on the Amazon product page. This adorable 16-inch animatronic Pikachu features 120 movements, lights, and sounds. Motion and touch trigger all the action. Think an old-school Furby but bigger and does more. 40% Off the LEGO Phantom Menace Battle Droid with STAP The LEGO Phantom Menace Battle Droid with STAP is 40% off, matching its Prime Big Deal days and all-time low pricing. This build features 1,088 pieces and is bigger than you’d expect, measuring over 15 inches. Once finished, a display stand, complete with a cute mini droid, lets you show off your build on a shelf or desk. Chainsaw Man Box Set Drops to Lowest Price of the Year Whether you’re looking to jump into a new manga series or want to add physical copies to your collection, the first Chainsaw Man box set is down to its lowest price of the year as an early Black Friday deal. The story follows Denji, an orphaned teen who fights local Devils, becomes a half-Devil himself, and joins a crew of government-run Devil Hunters. This box set collects the first 11 volumes of Chainsaw Man, covering the entire Public Safety arc. mFish 6.6ft 240W 4-in-1 USB Cable for $6.59 Want a versatile USB Type-C cable for cheap? The mFish 6.6ft 240W 4-in-1 USB cable is exactly what you need. Instead of just a USB-C to USB-C connection, this cable connects in four different ways: USB-C to USB-C, USB-C to USB-A, Lightning to USB-C, and Lightning to USB-A. The cable measures 6.6 feet, delivers up to 240W, and each end even lights up. Best of all, you can get the mFish cable for just $6.59 with the coupon code "4CJSX7O3". Pokémon TCG Invite Requests It’s back; you can request an invite to purchase the Pokémon TCG: 30th Celebration Elite Trainer Box for $59.99 on Amazon. That’s well below the market value, which is sitting around twice that amount. If you still want the ETB and don’t want to pay a fortune, it’s worth a shot. Even if you’re selected, you don’t have to buy. Keep checking your email; if selected, you'll have 72 hours to purchase. You can also enter a drawing at Target to get the 30th Celebration Booster Bundle for MSRP. Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution - Delta Reign dropped, and you can score a Booster Box at MSRP. You just need to request an invite at Best Buy now and a free Best Buy account to make the request. If selected, you’ll have 24 hours to make the purchase. The box includes 36 booster packs for $160.99, making each just $4.47, a steal in this market. AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D Is $399.99 Jumping into a new gaming PC build? The AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D is IGN’s top CPU , and it’s just $399.99 on Amazon when you clip the coupon. It's also available for the same price on Newegg with the code BFF36. This processor uses 3D V-Cache to reduce latency and allow for 96MB of L3 cache. Its overall performance is incredible for gaming, making it ideal for pairing with a powerful graphics card. The AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D even earned a 9/10 in IGN’s review , with reviewer Jackie Thomas calling it “the new king of gaming processors.” If you want a slight performance boost over the Ryzen 7 9800X3D, get the Ryzen 7 9850X3D for $419 when you clip the listed coupon on Amazon. MTG x Star Trek Play Booster Box Preorder Drops to New Low The MTG x Star Trek Play Booster Box preorder has just dropped to its lowest price yet on Amazon. For just $124.99, you’ll get 30 Play Boosters, bringing each to just $4.17. MTG’s latest Universes Beyond set is out later this week, but if the price drops further before then, Amazon offers an awesome preorder guarantee. 50% Off Criterion Collection 4K Blu-rays The Criterion Collection Early Black Friday Sale has dropped 4K Blu-ray prices by 50%. Cinephiles will want to jump on these physical media deals while you can because the most popular films and collections may sell out. Guillermo del Toro’s Frankenstein starring Oscar Isaac and Jacob Elordi, the incredibly popular animated movie KPop Demon Hunters, and even Godzilla: The Showa-Era Films are all discounted. Save $40 on the LEGO Pikachu and Poké Ball I feel like I keep posting this LEGO Pikachu and Poké Ball set, but now it’s at the lowest price I’ve seen: $159.95. It’s over 2,000 pieces and has tons of detail, including posable ears and limbs on Pikachu. It doesn’t stop there; the display stand is more intricate than a typical LEGO stand, featuring a lightning-bolt shape, Pikachu’s “25” Pokédex number, and a few electric sparks.
